root_cause: The existing protected migration-only terminal verifier checked only version values in Supabase migration history. It could therefore accept a misnamed migration record and did not prove the expected original ONE BRAIN trigger still existed and was enabled. Merged PR #5724 was not sufficient because production still had 842 applied migrations and the 083000 runtime trigger was absent in a read-only query.
prevention_rule: Use the SAME existing terminal postmerge verifier and authenticated Supabase provider query, compare the exact protected migration version plus name and reject duplicate or missing IDs. For original terminal-guard migration 083000 and all later migration-only releases, independently read back its enabled invoker-only trigger, restricted permissions and exact ACK/veto/outcome error classes. Never fake provider history, close a BRAIN obligation from mere CI, add a second scheduler or replay ambiguous provider sends. Original GitOps source-lock owner repairs and re-verifies under protected main.
evidence: 2026-11-13: PR #5724 was merged by GitHub; native Supabase production read-only schema_migrations had 842 applied (latest 082500), not new 083000, and pg_trigger had no original terminal-proof trigger.
Original cron #171 remained active; last observed run succeeded at 2026-11-13T08:56 UTC; 9 GREEN and 6 RED loops, 365 OPEN content handoffs. Cron succeeded is not downstream success.

Original migration-only terminal path is .github/workflows/obligation-terminal-closure.yml -> tools/delivery/supabase-migration-production-readback.mjs. Existing workflow preserved; no new writer or scheduler.

Regression tests cover same-version wrong-name, duplicate, absent/disabled trigger, expected true runtime, and subsequent migration after 083000. Production enforcement still requires protected merge and independent readback.
limitations: The verifier detects and blocks false-green; it is not a provider migration deployment or repair engine.
It runs when the existing protected terminal workflow verifies a migration-only release; 24/7 cron health remains under original #171/ONE BRAIN.
A green SQL guard is not the same as customer input, Instagram provider post, website conversion, paid revenue or learning outcome.
